title: Chapter 262: The Hanging Man [2 in 1]
html:
“I understand why the chairperson is targeting him. The man has probably passed through the door before. He may even possess a ‘door’ of his own.” Kong Xiangming kept his voice low, wary of unseen listeners.

“It doesn’t matter. So what if he has been behind the door? He is still only one man.” Wei Wu’s words lacked conviction; he seemed to be reassuring himself. “This mission is too important for the chairperson to send only us. Other society members are probably already here.”

“Don’t rely on anyone else. What if the chairperson intends to sacrifice us as scouts?” Kong Xiangming closed the door. “The society’s members may change at any time, but the numbers remain constant. Each corresponds to a monster from behind the door. Receiving a number means forming a bond with that monster. In the chairperson’s eyes, the monsters inside us matter—not the vessels carrying them.”

His eyes narrowed as he seemingly changed the subject. “The Ghost Stories Society forbids us from revealing our identities or investigating other members. Those rules protect us because the society is filled with madmen and murderers. But have you considered their other implication?”

“What other implication?”

“If we never interact, we can never discover the chairperson’s identity.” Kong Xiangming’s gaze deepened. “Everyone knows the chairperson sits among the ten people at the dining table, yet none of us knows which one he is. I have begun to suspect that he may be a monster from behind the door—and that we are merely vessels for creatures like him.”

“Why are you telling me this?” Wei Wu edged away. “No one has ever betrayed the Ghost Stories Society. That is the most frightening thing about it. Do you understand?”

Kong Xiangming shrugged. “We joined the society at the same time, so I know you aren’t the chairperson. That is why I approached you during our previous mission and revealed my identity. You are the only person in the society I can trust.”

Wei Wu sensed that Kong Xiangming was still withholding something. He wanted no part of the scheme, but it had already ensnared him.

“Every monster escaped from behind the door, so the chairperson must possess a door of his own.” A thin smile crossed Kong Xiangming’s face. “Whoever controls the door creates the rules. Don’t you want to become chairperson?”

“You really have lost your mind.”

“I haven’t. I simply have no ghost stories left to share. Unless the rules change, the next time we meet, I may be served on your plate—transformed from diner into dinner.” His words struck Wei Wu like ice water. The Ghost Stories Society offered no charity; even its own members feared its power.

“Tell me your plan.”

“I would never have risked this before, but a recent opportunity changed everything. The chairperson has been communicating with us more frequently. The more he involves himself, the more weaknesses he exposes.”

“What weakness?”

“The chairperson sends messages through the monsters possessing us, but those creatures can communicate only within fifty meters of one another. We have already tested the limit.” Kong Xiangming reached his central point. “In other words, whenever he contacted us, the chairperson was within fifty meters.”

“You’re right.”

“At every meeting, I sit near No. 10. Whenever he is close, the monster inside me experiences a strange hunger. It wants to devour him.”

“That doesn’t prove No. 10 is the chairperson. All ten of us carry different monsters.”

“I know. But several seconds before my monster received the chairperson’s message, it felt that same hunger.” Kong Xiangming’s voice slowly changed. “When the message arrived, both No. 10 and the chairperson were near my home. Doesn’t that prove a connection?”

“Could this be a coincidence?”

“The chairperson must be the one who sent our invitations. He alone knows every member’s true identity. On both occasions when he contacted me, No. 10 was near my home. No coincidence stretches that far.”

When Kong Xiangming finished, Wei Wu fell silent. The mysterious chairperson hung over every member like a blade poised at the neck.

“No. 10 is the chairperson? Then how do you expect us to cooperate?” Wei Wu walked beside Kong Xiangming. Their shared objective created a temporary truce; without that mutual interest, knowing each other’s identities would have made them mortal enemies.

“The chairperson wants this Haunted House’s boss dead, which means the man is dangerous. Let them fight each other while we wait for an opening.” Kong Xiangming entered the bathroom, lowered the female body from the ceiling, and removed a name tag from its pocket. “We came as visitors. Make sure the boss believes it.”

The pair left with the name tag. A minute or two later, something rolled across the floor inside the room.

A mannequin’s head emerged from beneath the bed.

…

The three medical students huddled together. Deprived of their map, they finally understood the true ‘joy’ of visiting a Haunted House.

“Li Xue, wait for us!” The baby-faced girl strode alone at the front. The two young men crowded so closely behind her that they might as well have held hands.

“Outside, you competed to see who could boast the loudest. Now that we’ve lost the seniors’ guide, why are you both so timid?” Li Xue glanced back and sighed. “Are you two even men?”

“What does this have to do with gender?” Though Wang Dan hid at the rear, his attitude remained defiant. “This is called caution. Can’t you see that we’re guarding your back?”

“Ha ha.”

Yang Chen flushed with embarrassment. “I’m not afraid. This place simply resembles my high school too closely. The earlier sets looked fake at a glance, but here I feel as though I’ve returned to school.”

“What is frightening about returning to high school?” Li Xue asked.

“When a set clearly differs from reality, I can remind myself that everything is fake. This place matches my memories so closely that, no matter what I tell myself, I cannot resist its atmosphere.” Still clutching his notebook and pen, Yang Chen mapped the route with trembling fingers.

For reasons unknown, most of Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy had been omitted, leaving the scenario relatively small. The students soon reached the corridor’s end, where an ordinary glass door awaited them.

“Wait!” Yang Chen stopped Li Xue before she opened it. He leaned closer and peered through the dusty glass. “This looks like a dormitory floor. The doors are even numbered.”

“Could this be the girls’ dormitory from the map?” Li Xue had Yang Chen compare the routes, but the locations differed too greatly.

“It must be a hidden scenario,” Yang Chen declared. “When I first saw the map, I wondered why it showed a girls’ dormitory but no boys’ dormitory. Apparently, the boys’ building was hidden. But how did we trigger it? We haven’t done anything unusual.”

“The boss probably panicked because we were clearing the map too quickly.” Wang Dan laughed smugly as he joined Yang Chen. “It resembles our dormitory. Let’s look inside.”

Despite his words, Wang Dan did not move. In the end, Li Xue pushed the door open. The rusted lock fell to the floor, and a peculiar odor seeped through the widening gap.

“Why does it smell like a decomposing body?”

“Should we even go in?”

“Honestly, discovering this hidden scenario already broke the seniors’ record.” Wang Dan raised a hand. “I suggest we leave while we still can.”

“We may not trigger it again. Since we’re already here, why not go inside? Are you really willing to turn back now?”

Yang Chen and Li Xue seized Wang Dan and dragged him into the corridor.

Half-open doors lined both sides of the dark corridor. The awful stench seemed to come from everywhere at once.

“This place is unnecessarily creepy.” Wang Dan lowered his voice, as though any louder sound might wake the monsters sleeping nearby.

“We still have time. We cannot ignore any rooms. This place must hide plenty of name tags.” Yang Chen walked at the front beside Li Xue. Wang Dan followed reluctantly. Deeply uneasy but too frightened to leave alone, he had no choice but to continue with them.

“Don’t be a coward. The worst scares are probably farther inside, so the first few rooms should be safe.” Yang Chen tried to reassure him with experience. “What Haunted House puts its most frightening scene at the entrance?”

As he spoke, he opened the first bedroom on the left. Dust cascaded from the wooden frame like a curtain, as though no one had entered for months. The door creaked inward. Yang Chen took one step and froze, his upper body leaning forward while his feet rooted themselves to the floor.

“Yang Chen? What’s wrong?” The door swung fully open, and Li Xue and Wang Dan drew sharp breaths. Someone hung in the center of the room.

“A mannequin?” Yang Chen recovered first and wiped his sweat-slick palms against his clothes.

“Don’t enter yet.” Wang Dan pointed at the figure’s feet. “It isn’t truly hanging; its feet are still on the floor. That may be a Haunted House actor.”

“I don’t think so.” The bravest of the group, Li Xue walked directly inside. “The rope is taut. Even with both feet on the ground, holding that posture would place enormous strain on the neck.”

She approached cautiously. The hanging figure wore a black coat and bowed its head, concealing its face. Li Xue slowly extended one finger until it touched the ‘corpse’s’ skin.

“It isn’t human skin. Come in—it’s safe.” An audible sigh of relief passed through the room. The figure had badly shaken all three.

“Why hang a mannequin in the middle of the room while leaving its feet on the floor?” Wang Dan touched the figure’s hand. As a forensic science student, he knew the difference between artificial and human skin; this felt colder and harder.

“Don’t touch things carelessly. The body may be part of a puzzle we haven’t found yet.” Li Xue gently lifted the figure’s chin. The sight of its face disturbed all three medical students.

It looks too real!

Because they had studied actual corpses, the resemblance frightened them far more than it would an ordinary visitor.

“The rope compressed the front of the neck, forcing the tongue upward and obstructing the throat and windpipe. The probable cause of death is asphyxiation.”

Li Xue surprised herself. She had never expected her first practical use of classroom knowledge to occur inside a Haunted House.

“Look closely at the face. Those irregular blood spots differ from ordinary asphyxiation.” Yang Chen circled the mannequin. “The broken neck interrupted blood flow to the brain. Cerebral ischemia was probably the true cause of death.”

“Does it matter how a mannequin died? We should focus on leaving!” Wang Dan urged. “A prop in a Haunted House doesn’t merely resemble a real corpse—it perfectly reproduces its cause of death. Doesn’t that frighten you?”

“Does the Haunted House’s boss know forensic science?” Li Xue looked toward Yang Chen.

Yang Chen’s expression worsened. “An amateur couldn’t reproduce a corpse’s distinctive features so perfectly… unless he used a real body as his model.”

The same image entered all three minds. Without a word, they left the bedroom in perfect unison.

“We’ve gone deep enough. How about leaving now?”

“Let’s inspect a few more rooms first. Did either of you notice a name tag in there?” Yang Chen asked. Li Xue and Wang Dan both shook their heads.

“Didn’t pay much attention.”

“Then we’ll search the other rooms and return to this one last.”

As the students discussed their strategy outside, none noticed the standing body behind them slowly open its eyes.

Another junction lay farther down the corridor. The deeper they ventured, the stronger the stench became.

Grimy stains spread across the tiles and walls. The students continued to the corridor’s end, where several rooms stood locked.

“The stench seems to come from here.” Walking in front, Li Xue opened the deepest room.

Four beds occupied the room, but only one held a mattress. Rubbish towered across the other three.

“That’s all? I expected something terrifying. The first bedroom was far worse than this.”

“We’re running out of time. Focus on the name tags. Wang Dan, stop daydreaming and help us!”

Yang Chen and Li Xue entered, leaving Wang Dan alone in the long, dark corridor. Somewhere behind him, something began hopping closer.

“Yang Chen, come out! I think I heard a fourth person’s footsteps.”
